newsitem.title: USA: US utility investors oppose open power market bill.
newsitem.headline: US utility investors oppose open power market bill.

text.p: Several utility investor groups came together Wednesday to oppose legislation in Congress that would make states break up electric utility monopolies.

Led by Bill Steinmeier, ex-chairman of the Missouri Public Service Commission, the Electric Utility Shareholders Association said the federal government should not force states to open local power markets to competition.
The investors fear their utility shares will lose value if all consumers are allowed to start choosing their own power suppliers and turning away from high-cost utilities.
The alliance said it would "resist attempts to drastically reconfigure the electric utility industry through intrusive Federal legislation."
"The affordability and reliability of electricity in this country has been made possible through vast expenditures of capital," Electric USA said in its statement of purpose.
"Small shareholders, literally millions of ordinary Americans through their pension funds, mutual fund holdings or as individual investors, have made these capital expenditures possible," it said.
Eight of the 32 groups in the alliance are from Colorado, home state of Republican Rep. Dan Schaefer who introduced the sweeping legislation this summer to restructure the electricity market.

Groups in Electric USA include the Colorado Cattlemen's Association, Rocky Mountain Farmers Union, Oklahoma Municipal League, Connecticut Association of Schools, and the Virginia Alliance of State Employees.
